main_text.p: um vita non excedere, quem vento-

um equorum conceptum Varro & Columella aliique recenfent. eodem edit, quod Plinius libr. xi. cap. 37. narrat, Pecora in Euboea Chalcide fel non habere, & uti fubdit, carent eo, qui abfynthio vefcuntur in Ponto, & quae funt iftius generis innumera; nisi huius Ariftotelem & Plinium ita velit interpretari, ipfos noluiffe folipedes & cervos omni prorfus bile carere, sed veficula duntaxat fellea deftitui, ut fane hanc ipforum mentem effe, vel hinc conftat, quia Plinius equorum fel virulentum effe docet libr. xviii. cap. 9. inquiens, inter omnia communia animalium vel praestantissimi affectus fel est, vis ejus, excalfacere, mordere, fcindere, extrahere, difcutere. minorum animalium subtilius intelligitur, & ideo ad oculorum medicamenta subtilius existimatur. taurino praecipua potentia, etiam in aere, pellibusque colore aureo ducendis. & paulo post: damnatur

page.notes: Printed text is partly damaged at the left edge and the first letters of several lines are cut off; readings such as "um", "ter" and "ur" are fragments of words cut by the scan edge. The line "tur" at the lower right is a catchword-like continuation of "damnatur" and is treated as its end. Some words in the original are uncertain due to blur (e.g. "minorum", "subtilius" repeated in the source).
